line: The smallest sheet: ·𐑥𐑱𐑯 (mayn) sends the text «𐑣𐑧𐑤𐑴 𐑢𐑻𐑤𐑛» (heloh wurld) to its output.
Four primitives on constants: 𐑑 multiplies and its mirror 𐑛 divides, 𐑚 subtracts, 𐑥 takes the smaller.
·𐑛𐑳𐑚𐑩𐑤 (dubəl) feeds its input into both arrowheads of 𐑐 (add), so 21 comes out 42.
03 · double sketched in ASCII with +--+ and -->. It means the same, and Format redraws it.
·𐑨𐑚𐑕 (abs): 𐑤 asks whether a number is below 0, and a switch passes it on or subtracts it from 0.
Nodes written inline, without boxes: 5 doubles twice, goes to text with 𐑖 and back with 𐑠, and doubles again.
𐑒 makes a pair and its mirror 𐑜 takes one apart. Two crossing wires swap the halves.
Three 𐑟 nodes build [1 2 3] onto 𐑯𐑦𐑤 (nil), and the mirror 𐑕 splits it into head and tail.
·𐑓𐑨𐑒𐑑 (fakt) calls itself in a switch arm, multiplying down to 1: the factorials of 10 and 20.
08 · factorial sketched in ASCII, its switch and dotted divider included.
·𐑤𐑧𐑙𐑔 (length) splits off a list's head with 𐑕 and adds 1 to the length of the rest.
·𐑒𐑬𐑯𐑑 (kownt) calls itself 100,000 times. Each is a tail call, so it runs in constant space.
·𐑰𐑝𐑩𐑯 (eevən) and ·𐑪𐑛 (od) call each other, each taking 1 away, until one reaches 0.
·𐑯𐑱𐑥 (naym) names a number: a switch with a guard on each arm, and a default arm for the rest.
One source branches to five arrowheads: 𐑐 doubles 7, 𐑑 squares it, 𐑖 and 𐑠 turn it to text and back.
𐑯𐑦𐑤 (nil), the empty list, drawn as a node box of its own.
One wire branches twice, and the branches cross on their way to two outputs.
The mirror pair 𐑗 and 𐑡: 𐑗 chops «𐑖𐑷𐑤𐑲𐑯» (shawlien) into letters, and 𐑡 joins them back.
An inline node's output branches: 𐑖 shows 42 as text, and 𐑠 reads one branch back as a number.
The reflected binary Gray code: ·𐑒𐑪𐑐𐑦 (kopi) puts «0» before each shorter code, ·𐑥𐑦𐑮𐑼 (mirər) «1» before them reversed.
